hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of a squared and a length of negative three a. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative ten a and the length is negative three a. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of twenty five with a length of negative three a.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{-3a}(a^2-10a+25)
\\\\
&=\goldE{-3a}(a^2)+(\goldE{-3a})(-10a)+(\goldE{-3a})(25)
\\\\
&=-3a^3+30a^2-75a
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of a squared and a length of negative three a. Inside of this rectangle is negative three a cubed. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative ten a and the length is negative three a. Inside of this rectangle is thirty a squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of twenty five with a length of negative three a. Inside of this rectangle is negative seventy five a.
